lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the shared Campanulaceae framework—fused corolla, inferior ovary, 5-part flowers and secondary pollen presentation—then split the project into a Triodanis free-stamen/pore-capsule door and a Lobelia anther-tube/bilabiate door.

project_scope.selection_mode: Project module across Triodanis and Lobelia
project_scope.note: Six source rows represent five species-level concepts plus one accepted infraspecific concept: source Triodanis biflora is currently treated by Kew as Triodanis perfoliata subsp. biflora.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Find a single flower—not a composite head—and inspect the ovary position. In the project genera the corolla is fused and the ovary is inferior, with the other flower parts arising above it.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Mostly herbs in the project pool, with simple alternate leaves. Milky latex is common in Campanulaceae but is not needed as a crew field test.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually 5-merous with a sympetalous corolla and an inferior ovary containing many ovules. Five stamens are present, but their relationship differs sharply by project genus: free in Triodanis, anthers connate into a tube around the style in Lobelia.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Capsule with many seeds in the project taxa. Triodanis capsules open by pores in the lower portion; Lobelia cardinalis has an apically valvate capsule.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: First confirm individual fused-corolla flowers over an inferior ovary. Then ask: regular/star-like with free stamens = Triodanis; strongly bilabiate with an anther tube = Lobelia.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: inferior ovary → fused 5-part corolla → Triodanis door → Lobelia door → pollen-presentation mechanism → capsule openings → taxonomy cleanup
visual_lesson.intro: Campanulaceae makes more sense if the learner stops expecting every member to look like a bell. Our local pool contains both a fairly regular Venus's-looking-glass flower and the radically asymmetric cardinal flower.

steps.title: 1 · Locate the inferior ovary
steps.look_for: The corolla, calyx and stamens arise above the ovary; the ovary is embedded below the visible flower.
steps.why_it_matters: This is a strong family-level Asterales character shared by both project genera.

steps.title: 2 · Triodanis door: regular flower + free stamens
steps.photo_role: Triodanis flower face and opened flower
steps.look_for: A blue-purple rotate to shallowly campanulate flower usually divided into 5 lobes, with 5 stamens free from one another; lower axils may also contain tiny cleistogamous flowers.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates Venus's-looking-glass from Lobelia without relying on color.

steps.title: 3 · Find the Triodanis pore-opening capsule
steps.look_for: An elongated inferior capsule opening through 2–3 pores in the lower part of the fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: A highly memorable genus-level fruit character after the showy corolla is gone.

steps.title: 4 · Lobelia door: split two-lipped corolla
steps.look_for: The corolla is split nearly to the base dorsally and forms a bilabiate limb: 2 upper lobes and 3 lower lobes.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains why cardinal flower looks so different from Triodanis while remaining in the same family.

steps.title: 5 · Find the Lobelia anther tube
steps.look_for: Five anthers joined into a tube around the style; the reproductive column projects through the dorsal corolla split.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the key Lobelia mechanism and a major contrast with free-stamen Triodanis.

steps.title: 6 · Show plunger pollen presentation
steps.look_for: The style pushes pollen through the anther tube, then the receptive 2-lobed stigma emerges later.
steps.why_it_matters: Turns an abstract Asterales pollen-presentation concept into a visible sequence.

steps.title: 7 · Clean up Triodanis biflora
steps.look_for: Source Triodanis biflora → accepted Triodanis perfoliata subsp. biflora under current Kew.
steps.why_it_matters: Avoids counting the subspecies as a separate species while preserving the familiar source name.

comparisons.title: Campanulaceae vs Asteraceae
comparisons.rule: Both are Asterales and commonly have inferior ovaries plus secondary pollen presentation. Campanulaceae project flowers are individual fused-corolla flowers producing many-seeded capsules; Asteraceae packs many tiny florets into a capitulum and each floret usually makes a one-seeded cypsela.

comparisons.title: Triodanis vs Lobelia
comparisons.rule: Triodanis = more regular 5-lobed flower, free stamens, lower-axil cleistogamous flowers and a pore-opening capsule. Lobelia = strongly zygomorphic 2+3 corolla, connate anther tube around the style and an apically valvate capsule.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not teach Campanulaceae as 'bell-shaped blue flowers.' Corolla symmetry and stamen architecture vary strongly between the project genera; inferior ovary plus fused-corolla/reproductive architecture is the better family framework.
